name: Shenzhen Megmeet Electrical Co., Ltd. (深圳麦格米特电气股份有限公司)
employees: 8,894 (filed, 2025-12-31); more than 3,400 R&D engineers, 34.6% of headcount, per the H1 2026 interim
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Megmeet's rack-power business is shipping and growing, but the product that would put it above the rack — the solid-state transformer — remains a research programme with no disclosed voltage class, and the company told investors in August 2026 that its sales for the next two to three years will come from its existing product matrix. BACKGROUND: Shenzhen-based power-electronics and electrical-automation manufacturer, listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange since 2017 (SZSE: 002851, per the H1 2026 interim cover), organised in six business groups — 电源产品 power products (including AI data-centre and network power), 智慧生活 smart living, 新能源交通 new-energy transport, 工业自动化 industrial automation, 智能装备 intelligent equipment and 磁电精造 magnetics and precision connection. H1 2026 (interim, 28 August 2026): revenue RMB 6.061B (+29.68%); power products RMB 1.841B (+60.92%) at a 25.06% gross margin, +2.62pp — the only one of the three largest segments to expand its margin (magnetics and intelligent equipment also expanded; smart living fell 4.33pp). Earnings quality weakened: attributable net profit +45.21% but ex-non-recurring net profit −16.13%, the gap being RMB 133.88M of non-recurring items led by RMB 137.35M of fair-value gains, with operating cash flow −84.62%. FY2025: revenue RMB 9.403B (+15.05%), attributable net profit RMB 145.8M (−66.58%), R&D RMB 1.122B (11.94% of revenue). Corporate: an HKEX A1 for an A+H listing was filed 26 June 2026 and, as of 23 September, has no hearing and no CSRC filing notice on record; on 22 September the board agreed to buy the 46.30% minority of its welding subsidiary for RMB 663.64M cash. Next report: Q3 2026, due by the 31 October 2026 statutory deadline.
ecosystemRole: We assess Megmeet as a qualified challenger in NVIDIA-class rack power that is, on the public record, unranked — and not yet a hall-edge vendor. Basis, per company filings: the H1 2026 interim calls it 「英伟达（NVIDIA Corporation）指定的数据中心电源推荐提供商之一」, and the November 2025 exchange inquiry reply specifies what that means — it 「进入其向下游客户的推荐名单」, a place on the list NVIDIA recommends to its downstream customers, not direct sales to NVIDIA. NVIDIA's own October 2025 ecosystem post lists Megmeet under power system components with Bizlink, Delta, Flex, Lead Wealth and LITEON, not under data-centre power systems, where the medium-voltage and SST vendors sit. The company itself told investors in April 2026 that it was late on GB200 and won limited orders there, then won batch orders on GB300 that contributed from Q1 2026. Per broker research, Soochow (April 2026) expects it to become NVIDIA's third NVL72 PSU source after Delta and LITEON; per MTC's independent 2024 ranking it is third in global OEM/embedded power-supply sales at about US$1.17B, a figure inside LITEON's estimated range. It publishes the full grid-to-GPU chain — sidecar racks rectifying 380–480 VAC to 800 VDC at over 1 MW per rack, power, BBU and capacitor shelves, CRPS/M-CRPS PSUs, PDB and Power Brick — but its SST is under R&D with no stated input voltage. Against Delta and LITEON it is the challenger in the same component tier; against the hall-edge specialists it is a rack vendor reaching upward.

productsAndServices.name: Power Products — AI Data-Center & Network Power
productsAndServices.category: Power electronics · 28.5% of FY2025 revenue (22.33% gross margin); 30.4% of H1 2026 revenue (25.06%)
productsAndServices.description: Server and data-centre power across three layers the company names in its H1 2026 interim: outside the rack (800 VDC sidecar/side racks, and a solid-state transformer under R&D), energy-storage compensation (AC EDPP compensator, BBU and supercapacitor shelves, a DC-centre BESS), and inside the rack (33 kW and 110 kW power shelves, an 800 V→50 V DC-DC shelf, CRPS/M-CRPS PSUs, PDB and Power Brick). Also telecom/network power, medical and industrial PSUs, display power, 54 V→12 V board-mount DC-DC modules, and PV/storage/EV-charging modules.
highlights: NVIDIA status, per filings: 「英伟达（NVIDIA Corporation）指定的数据中心电源推荐提供商之一」 (H1 2026 interim); the November 2025 exchange inquiry reply specifies a place on NVIDIA's list recommended to its downstream customers. NVIDIA's October 2025 ecosystem post lists it under power system components

Customer record, per company: GB200 — 「布局进度较晚，获取订单数量有限」; GB300 — batch orders won, contributing from Q1 2026; Vera Rubin products in testing with several North American cloud customers (IR record, 29 April 2026)

Delivery, per the H1 2026 interim: AIDC products began batch, continuing delivery from Q1 2026 across technology owners, system integrators and cloud operators; in H1 2026 batch delivery began to project demand from 「部分北美大客户」. No customer named; details withheld under NDA

No data-centre revenue line is disclosed. FY2025: AIDC power had no material effect on full-year results (company); H1 2026: within power products' +60.92%, data-centre and network power grew most (IR record, 28 August 2026)
Named network-power customers (filings): Ericsson, Cisco, Juniper, Arista, Accton, plus an unnamed 「北美AI大客户」 — no entity, contract or ship-to geography disclosed

Lab accreditations CNAS, TÜV, UL-WTDP and UL-CTF (in-house testing programmes); product-level safety marks on CRPS/M-CRPS datasheets include UL — no UL or ETL file number published for any data-centre product
Dallas, Texas AI data-centre power test lab opened June 2026 (company-owned, up to 360 kW active validation, roadmap toward 1.5 MW)
productsAndServices.positioning: Per the company, the market was long dominated by Taiwanese suppliers and it is 'gradually breaking' that position; it states no rank or share. Independent context: MTC ranks it third in 2024 global OEM/embedded power-supply sales (about US$1.17B) behind Delta and LITEON, whose estimated range it falls inside; Soochow (April 2026) estimates Delta above 70% of NVIDIA's 2025 power supply and expects Megmeet to become the third NVL72 PSU source; TrendForce (March 2026) says its share 'is still expected to take time to build'. The oft-repeated claim that it displaced LITEON as NVIDIA's number-two power-shelf source traces to early-2025 market rumour and has no supporting source.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Two routes, per the company (IR record, 29 April 2026): power shelves, BBU and related parts to server manufacturers who integrate and ship the rack, and direct supply to end customers. A Goldman Sachs note relayed by Sina (April 2026) says the first GB300 volume order came through a US-headquartered ODM for a North American CSP; the ODM is not named
productsAndServices.targetSegments: AI data centres (NVIDIA-architecture racks and domestic hyperscalers), telecom and networking OEMs, medical devices, industrial equipment, EV charging
productsAndServices.roadmap: Vera Rubin: 110 kW liquid-cooled 3RU shelf (VR200) and 33 kW supercapacitor shelf in validation — the company expects Vera Rubin products to be its largest AIDC demand overseas in the next one to two years. 800 V→50 V 90 kW 1RU shelf in validation. SST: under R&D; the company expects no rapid market ramp for one to two years and says sales for the next two to three years will come from existing products (IR record, 28 August 2026). Dallas lab expansion toward 1.5 MW.

recentDevelopments.headline: Agreed to buy the 46.30% minority of its welding subsidiary for RMB 663.64M cash
recentDevelopments.read: Consolidates the highest-margin group (38.51% FY2025 GM) at an equity value of RMB 1.456B with a three-year RMB 405M profit commitment — cash committed to the non-AI base while the AI build-out is still being funded. Not a related-party deal and no shareholder vote required.

recentDevelopments.headline: 54 V→12 V quarter-brick DC-DC modules (1.6 kW continuous / 2.4 kW peak, and 2 kW), up to 98.3% peak efficiency
recentDevelopments.read: Fills the board-level step below the power shelf — the same layer Vicor and the silicon vendors sell into.

recentDevelopments.headline: IR record: SST demand not expected to ramp for 1–2 years; sales for 2–3 years to come from the existing product matrix
recentDevelopments.read: The company's own statement that the SST is a later-decade option, not a near-term revenue line; Vera Rubin products are expected to be the largest overseas AIDC demand over the next one to two years.

recentDevelopments.headline: H1 2026 interim: revenue +29.68%, headline profit +45.21%, ex-non-recurring profit −16.13%
recentDevelopments.read: The AI leg is real — power products +60.92% with margin up 2.62pp, overseas +45.49% — but the profit headline is majority non-recurring and operating cash flow fell 84.62%. The interim dates the start of AIDC batch delivery to Q1 2026 across its customer chain and, separately, says batch delivery to some North American major customers began in H1 2026; it names no AI customer. Soochow called the business in line; Guosen cut its FY2026 profit forecast.

recentDevelopments.headline: Headquarters-base project deferred from September 2026 to December 2027
recentDevelopments.read: Not a capacity or AIDC slip: the project is a Shenzhen Nanshan district government-coordinated multi-party build, and the interim states the property has not been delivered to the company. Funded from the 2019 convertible bond, not the 2026 placement.

recentDevelopments.headline: Exchange unusual-movement notice after a >20% cumulative closing-price fall over 28–30 July; close of RMB 96.77 on 30 July, about 49% below the 22 June closing high
recentDevelopments.read: The AI-power premium is fragile. The company reported no undisclosed matters and said the controlling shareholder did not trade; 30.15M placement shares unlocked on 6 August.

recentDevelopments.headline: 40 kW AC-DC and DC-DC EV-charging module platform launched
recentDevelopments.read: Keeps the PV/storage/charging leg current while the AI story dominates — up to 1000V output, 127-module parallel.

recentDevelopments.headline: HKEX application proof (A1) filed for an H-share listing; joint sponsors Huatai Financial Holdings (Hong Kong) and Citigroup Global Markets Asia
recentDevelopments.read: Offshore capital to fund AI-power capex. As of 23 September the HKEX record shows only the A1 and two overall-coordinator notices (CICC HK and CMBI added 8 July) — no hearing, no CSRC filing notice. We assess the funding need as structural given weak operating cash flow.

recentDevelopments.headline: Opened AI data-center power testing lab in Dallas, Texas (360 kW, roadmap to 1.5 MW)
recentDevelopments.read: Validation capacity physically next to US hyperscaler customers — a localization signal beyond 'made in Thailand'.

recentDevelopments.headline: NVIDIA MGX support: 110 kW liquid-cooled power shelf, 800VDC rack conversion, BBU/supercap shelves
recentDevelopments.read: Productizing for GB300/Vera Rubin-class racks — moving up from 33 kW shelves to the liquid-cooled 110 kW class.

recentDevelopments.headline: Earnings-call IR record describes the SST as in pre-research (预研), grid high-voltage input to 800 VDC, no voltage class

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Megmeet is running an incumbent-funded pivot: the appliance-controls base (37.9% of FY2025 revenue) and the diversified industrial lines bankroll the AI data-centre power push. Basis: R&D of RMB 1.122B in FY2025 (11.94% of revenue) and above 10% of revenue for more than a decade per filings, with FY2025 ex-non-recurring profit down 92.96% while the 800 VDC chain was built. The 22 September 2026 welding buy-out shows the base is still being invested in, not harvested.

(Moderate confidence) We assess its position in NVIDIA-class rack power is a qualified third source, not a number two. Basis: the company says it was late on GB200 and won limited orders, then won GB300 batch orders; Soochow (April 2026) expects it to become the third NVL72 PSU source after Delta and LITEON; TrendForce (March 2026) says its share will take time to build. The claim that it displaced LITEON as the number-two power-shelf source traces to two early-2025 pieces that label it rumour (Sohu, 10 February 2025; 产业家, 13 March 2025); the company declined to confirm it when asked directly in December 2024; the ~41% Delta share attached to it was found in no source; and no 2026 ranking by TrendForce, DigiTimes or SemiAnalysis names Megmeet. Collection gap: no independent NVIDIA power-shelf share table for 2026 exists in the record.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the SST is an option on the next decade, not a product, and that Megmeet's hall-edge claim should be read that way. Basis: the company describes it as under R&D (预研 in May, 研发中 in August), narrowed its efficiency wording from an unqualified 'above 98.5%' in the April annual report to 'expected' in the June HKEX proof and the August interim, and says SST demand will not ramp for one to two years and that sales for two to three years will come from existing products. Collection gap: no voltage class is disclosed in any filing, IR record, product page or brochure; a single press report (ifeng, 1 July 2026) of a '10 kV domestic / 35 kV overseas' plan cites an earnings call whose exchange-filed record contains no kV figure.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the US footprint is a localisation and validation presence rather than a production base the company is prepared to put in its filings. Basis: its website places a 35,000 sq ft 'U.S. manufacturing base' in Richardson, Texas, and a Texas licensing record shows a 39,200 sq ft Megmeet renovation at 2821 Telecom Parkway, Richardson, registered in May 2024; but the HKEX proof lists six manufacturing bases with none in the US and describes the US subsidiary as sales and international operations, and the 2026 placement funds no US plant. The filed tariff mitigation is Thailand. Whether the June 2026 Dallas test lab sits in the Richardson facility is not stated.

(High confidence) The market is underwriting a heavily second-half-weighted 2026 that the Q3 report will test. Basis: H1 attributable profit was RMB 252.1M, of which RMB 133.9M non-recurring, against a 15-institution FY2026 consensus mean of RMB 787M (range 515–937M, 同花顺, 23 September 2026) — implying about RMB 535M in H2. Soochow called H1 in line; Guosen cut its FY2026 forecast to RMB 652M from 780M on competition and FX. No AI-data-centre revenue line exists to check the ramp against; the power-products group is the only proxy.

relationships.note: NVIDIA lists Megmeet among its 800 VDC power-system-component partners; the company's filings call it one of NVIDIA's recommended data-centre power suppliers.
relationships.context:
Megmeet sits in the power-system-components tier of NVIDIA's published 800 VDC ecosystem with Bizlink, Delta, Flex, Lead Wealth and LITEON, and is not in the data-centre power systems tier where the medium-voltage and SST vendors sit. Its November 2025 exchange inquiry reply defines the relationship as a place on the list NVIDIA recommends to its downstream customers — not direct sales to NVIDIA.

Product history, per the company: an 800 V HVDC sidecar for the Kyber rack-scale platform (>1 MW per rack) announced May 2025 and shown at OCP in October 2025 as a collaboration with NVIDIA; MGX support including a 110 kW liquid-cooled shelf by May 2026. Commercially it was late on GB200 and won limited orders there, then won GB300 batch orders that contributed from Q1 2026; Vera Rubin products are in testing with North American cloud customers.

relationships.note: Competing second and third sources behind Delta in NVIDIA power supply; research places LITEON second and Megmeet a prospective third.
relationships.context:
Both sit in NVIDIA's 800 VDC power-system-components tier. The claim that Megmeet displaced LITEON as the number-two NVL72 power-shelf source traces to early-2025 pieces that label it market rumour, was never confirmed by Megmeet, and has no supporting source; Soochow (April 2026) instead expects Megmeet to become the third source after Delta and LITEON, and TrendForce (March 2026) names Delta and LITEON as the leading suppliers.

MTC's CY2024 ranking of all OEM/embedded power-supply sales puts LITEON second and Megmeet third, with Megmeet's roughly US$1.17B inside LITEON's estimated range. 36Kr (April 2025) separately expected Megmeet to take the largest share of NVIDIA's power-rack (sidecar) segment on first-mover grounds — a different product from the power shelf.

relationships.note: The incumbent in NVIDIA power supply; Soochow estimates Delta above 70% of NVIDIA's 2025 supply.
relationships.context:
Delta is the benchmark Megmeet's server-power push chases. Soochow (April 2026) estimates Delta's 2025 NVIDIA share above 70% and puts global 2024 server-PSU share at Delta 18% and LITEON about 12%, citing third-party market research; MTC ranks Delta first in 2024 OEM/embedded power-supply sales at several times Megmeet's.

Megmeet's wedge is architecture timing — first among mainland vendors on the 800 VDC sidecar chain — not share. Delta also carries a published 10 kV SST; Megmeet's SST is under R&D with no stated voltage class.

relationships.note: NVIDIA names Megmeet and Flex Power in the same power-system-components tier of its published 800 VDC ecosystem.
relationships.context:
Typed on the platform owner's own categorisation: both appear in one named tier of one named architecture, alongside Bizlink, Delta, Lead Wealth and LITEON.

The limit of the evidence is stated rather than glossed. There is no bilateral source, no matching product-announcement pair, and no ranking firm placing the two in a common share table.

The two are also differently shaped competitors. Megmeet contests the NVIDIA power-shelf socket as a power-electronics manufacturer; Flex arrives at the same socket as a contract manufacturer that has spent about $6.3bn since 2021 acquiring switchgear, cooling and power-conversion businesses, and has announced it will separate the whole segment into an independent company in early 2027.

relationships.note: Infineon silicon in Megmeet's 5.5 kW AI-server PSU platform.
relationships.context: A distributor re-post of an Infineon story reports Megmeet's 5.5 kW AI-server PSU uses Infineon CoolMOS 8 and OptiMOS 6 MOSFETs and CoolSiC devices. Infineon's own release was not opened; treat the specific part list as the distributor's account. Infineon speakers also appeared at Megmeet's September 2026 supplier conference.

relationships.note: Tier-one server-PSU and domestic HVDC competitor in Chinese broker mapping.
relationships.context: Soochow's November 2025 thematic counts Vertiv with Zhonhen and Delta at about 95% of China's 2025 data-centre HVDC market; its April 2026 note places Vertiv with Delta and LITEON in the first tier of China's server-PSU suppliers and Megmeet in the second. No bilateral source links the two companies.

relationships.note: China's data-centre HVDC leader; Megmeet is a domestic HVDC challenger.
relationships.context: Soochow's November 2025 thematic puts Zhonhen, Delta and Vertiv at about 95% of China's 2025 data-centre HVDC market and lists Megmeet among the domestic power vendors contesting it. No bilateral source links the two companies.

policyExposure.exposure: The exchange's November 2025 inquiry asked Megmeet to address US 'reciprocal tariff' and trade-friction risk to its overseas revenue. Its filings name production in China and Thailand, with Indian delivery through local contract manufacturers, and no US production base.
policyExposure.mitigation: Per the H1 2026 interim, using its Thailand factory capacity 「可很大程度上规避对美关税问题」; Thailand phase II is funded from the 2026 placement. The company website separately describes a Richardson, Texas manufacturing base that the filings do not list.

periods.commentary: Quality of earnings is the story, not the headline. Attributable net profit rose 45.21% while ex-non-recurring net profit fell 16.13%; the gap is RMB 133.88M of non-recurring items, dominated by RMB 137.35M of fair-value and disposal gains on financial assets — the wealth-management products holding RMB 1.65B of the January 2026 private placement. Operating cash flow fell 84.62%. Segment mix is where the AI leg shows: power products RMB 1.841B (+60.92%, 30.38% of revenue) with gross margin UP 2.62pp to 25.06%, against smart living RMB 2.557B (42.19%) with margin DOWN 4.33pp to 18.39%. Direct overseas revenue RMB 2.180B (+45.49%, 35.97% of revenue, 25.89% margin) grew at roughly double the domestic rate; the company puts direct plus indirect overseas above 43%. No AI-data-centre or data-centre revenue line is disclosed anywhere in the interim — the finest granularity published is the power-products aggregate. Consolidated gross margin is not printed; computed from the disclosed revenue and cost lines it is 21.21% against 22.07% a year earlier. Segment margins: three of six groups expanded (power products 25.06%, magnetics and precision connection 8.79%, intelligent equipment 39.67%); smart living fell 4.33pp to 18.39%. Financial expenses of RMB 93.70M were mainly FX losses. No interim dividend. Next report: Q3 2026, due by the 2026-10-31 statutory deadline; Q3 2025 was published 2025-10-30 and no appointment date or preliminary estimate is on record as of 2026-09-23.

periods.commentary: Verdicts split: Soochow Securities called FY2025 plus Q1 2026 'slightly above market expectations' excluding FX; the TradingView aggregator shows a −33% EPS miss. The company attributes about RMB 60M of the ex-non-recurring shortfall mainly to FX losses on INR and USD. Power products grew 66% (company, IR record 29 April 2026). Inventory +32% and receivables +18% show the AI ramp being pre-built.

financials.commentary: Forward consensus (同花顺, 15 institutions over six months, 2026-09-23): FY2026 attributable net profit mean RMB 787M (range 515–937M) on revenue of RMB 13.24B; FY2027 RMB 1.586B; FY2028 RMB 2.439B. Eastmoney shows 14 rating institutions — 7 Buy, 6 Add, 1 Neutral. Stock context: closing high RMB 188.79 on 2026-06-22 (intraday RMB 189.98 on 06-23) → RMB 96.77 close on 07-30, about −49%, prompting an exchange unusual-movement notice → RMB 122.85 on 2026-09-23 (about RMB 71.9B market value, derived from 585.01M shares). H-share A1 filed 2026-06-26 and still pending, with no hearing on record. Controlling group (Tong Yongsheng and spouse Wang Ping) at 23.08% on 2026-06-30, down from 28.68% in 2020 through sales, conversions and dilution. Guarantee quota above RMB 6B flagged by sell-side commentary as contingent risk.
